accessibility: Every field has a name (a row's fields are named for assistive technology only); an error is a line of text with an icon, never color alone; read-only state and the missing permission key are said in words next to an icon.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Icon, Badge, Button, NavItem, Select, SelectOption, TextInput, Table, TableRow, Divider, Alert, Skeleton, NumberField, Menu, MenuItem); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The real page has no setting for the requirements provider or its noUi list, and none is modelled here; the width and height fields are NumberFields, and the Workspace pages sub-navigation and the scroll-spy are not modelled.

Every visible string of the page is bound with $i18n except keys, labels, sizes, the file name and Locale tags, which are Workspace content; the sentence about a Locale file that does not exist is a baked sample per Locale because it names a link.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A member opened Settings from the Workspace pages; the three sections General, Viewports and Themes read from the Workspace settings file.
The base state is a desktop layout for a holder of settings.write: the primary Locale en-US, three viewports and two themes, nothing edited.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; on tablet and phone the page is read-only and says to edit on desktop, and a phone has no section index.
spec.intent: Show the Workspace settings page as built from Adapter Widgets only: the primary Locale, the viewports and the themes of the Workspace, each section saved on its own, with the section index.
interactionRules: General sets the primary Locale, explicitly: UIUX never infers it from the files or the selection, a tag that is not a language tag is refused, and a tag with no Locale file says so and points to Locales to create it.

Viewports list the canvas sizes widest first, each with a key (its identity, in mono), a label and a width and height; Themes list a key and a label; Add viewport and Add theme add a row whose key is typed inline.

A row needs a key without spaces that no other row uses, and a viewport a width and height of at least 1; a saved key is renamed or removed through the reference-impact check, never by typing over it.

Each section saves on its own with its own revision: its footer shows the number of unsaved changes with Discard and Save changes, a conflict keeps the draft and offers Reload theirs and Compare, and a lease held by someone else shows who and until when.
A member without settings.write sees the page read-only and is told which key is missing; the section index marks a section with unsaved changes.
